authors: Zifan Ning; Can Li; He Chen; Guangyao Zhou; Shanghang Zhang; Lianlin Li; Yin Zhuang
title: Uncertainty-Aware Cross-Domain Few-Shot Scene Classification from Remote Sensing Imagery
main_finding: Uses predictive uncertainty to improve robustness and knowledge transfer under remote-sensing domain discrepancy.
limitation: Few-shot target-domain setting differs from our source-only DG protocol.
relevance_to_our_work: Very recent evidence that domain discrepancy and uncertainty remain central RS classification problems.

authors: Sara A. Al-Emadi; Yin Yang; Ferda Ofli
title: Analysing Satellite Imagery Classification under Spatial Domain Shift across Geographic Regions
method: DG benchmark; ERM; modern DG methods; foundation models
evaluation_protocol: Single- and multi-source geographic domain-shift testing
main_finding: Shows significant geographic distribution shift and reports that carefully configured ERM with strong representations can remain highly competitive with modern DG methods.
limitation: Satellite geographic shift differs from our composite UAV/satellite/source shift.
relevance_to_our_work: One of the closest recent studies to our central finding that DG interventions do not automatically beat ERM.

authors: Abhishek Kuriyal; Elliot Vincent; Mathieu Aubry; Loic Landrieu
title: CoDEx: Combining Domain Expertise for Spatial Generalization in Satellite Image Analysis
main_finding: Shows domain-expert specialization and selection can improve spatial generalization across satellite datasets.
limitation: Different task/data regime and a more specialized multi-expert architecture.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent spatial-generalization comparison for satellite imagery.

authors: Yunxiao Qi; Dongyang Liu; Junping Zhang; Ye Zhang
title: A Shift Reduction Domain Generalization Network for Hyperspectral Image Cross-Domain Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Proposes explicit feature/domain-shift reduction for hyperspectral cross-domain classification.
limitation: Hyperspectral spectral-spatial setting differs from RGB aerial scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Very recent remote-sensing DG evidence demonstrating continued interest in unseen-domain robustness.

authors: Kim VanExel; Samendra Sherchan; Siyan Liu
title: Optimizing Deep Learning Models for Climate-Related Natural Disaster Detection from UAV Images and Remote Sensing Data
main_finding: Demonstrates strong deep-learning performance for Flooded, Desert, and Neither classification on the Climate Change Dataset.
limitation: Does not provide the provenance-aware, source-disjoint, multi-seed, external-validation failure analysis used in our study.
relevance_to_our_work: Original publication for the exact primary dataset and the direct baseline literature our work extends.

authors: Z. Han; C. Zhang; L. Gao; Z. Zeng; M. K. Ng; B. Zhang; J. Chanussot
title: Multi-Source Collaborative Domain Generalization for Cross-Scene Remote Sensing Image Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
method: Multi-source collaborative DG with adversarial augmentation and model diversification
main_finding: Reports improved cross-scene generalization through multi-source augmentation and diversification.
limitation: Uses a specialized multisource DG architecture and different data assumptions from our simpler interventions.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct recent remote-sensing DG comparison.

authors: Yang Li; Zhang Li; Ang Su; Kun Wang; Zi Wang; Qifeng Yu
title: Semisupervised Cross-Domain Remote Sensing Scene Classification via Category-Level Feature Alignment Network
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Uses category-level alignment to reduce cross-domain feature discrepancies.
limitation: Uses labeled/unlabeled target-domain information, unlike our target-unseen source-disjoint DG setting.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent comparison showing another strategy for cross-domain scene robustness.

authors: Yuchi Ma; Shuo Chen; Stefano Ermon; David B. Lobell
title: Transfer Learning in Environmental Remote Sensing
method: Review of transfer-learning approaches and domain shifts
main_finding: Systematizes domain-shift types and transfer-learning strategies in environmental remote sensing.
limitation: Review rather than a controlled benchmark of our specific climate-scene task.
relevance_to_our_work: Primary theoretical support for using pretrained backbones and discussing environmental domain shift.

authors: Deng Xinjie; Burhan Khan; Fazal Ghaffar; Yit Hong Choo; Tao Zhou
title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification and Its Application to UAV-based Disaster Management
main_finding: Demonstrates a lightweight feature-extraction design for UAV disaster-management classification.
limitation: Does not center source-domain generalization or external cross-source validation.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent disaster-classification comparison and deployment-oriented UAV context.

authors: Teng Yang; Song Xiao; Jiahui Qu; Wenqian Dong; Qian Du; Yunsong Li
title: Graph Embedding Interclass Relation-Aware Adaptive Network for Cross-Scene Classification of Multisource Remote Sensing Data
method: Graph embedding and interclass relation-aware adaptation
main_finding: Models class relationships and domain discrepancies for multisource cross-scene classification.
limitation: Unsupervised DA relies on target-domain samples.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the importance of multisource domain structure and class-aware cross-domain evaluation.

authors: Juepeng Zheng; Yibin Wen; Mengxuan Chen; Shuai Yuan; Weijia Li; Yi Zhao; Wenzhao Wu; Lixian Zhang; Runmin Dong; Haohuan Fu
title: Open-set Domain Adaptation for Scene Classification Using Multi-adversarial Learning
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Addresses cross-domain remote-sensing classification when target domains include unknown classes.
limitation: Open-set DA assumes access to target-domain data and a different label-space problem from our DG protocol.
relevance_to_our_work: Helps distinguish DG from broader real-world cross-domain adaptation settings.

authors: Peng Zhu; Xiangrong Zhang; Xiao Han; Xina Cheng; Jing Gu; Puhua Chen; Licheng Jiao
title: Cross-Domain Classification Based on Frequency Component Adaptation for Remote Sensing Images
dataset: AID; CLRS; MLRSN; RSSCN7; NWPU-RESISC45; NaSC-TG2
main_finding: Shows frequency-aware feature alignment can improve cross-domain remote-sensing scene classification.
limitation: Domain adaptation uses target-domain information; our primary DG setting assumes unseen target domains.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful contrast between domain adaptation and true target-unseen domain generalization.

authors: Kaiyang Zhou; Ziwei Liu; Yu Qiao; Tao Xiang; Chen Change Loy
title: Domain Generalization: A Survey
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
main_finding: Defines DG formally and organizes methods including alignment, meta-learning, augmentation, and ensembles.
limitation: Broad survey rather than remote-sensing-specific evidence.
relevance_to_our_work: Primary reference for defining DG and distinguishing it from transfer learning and domain adaptation.

authors: Ishaan Gulrajani; David Lopez-Paz
title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
method: DomainBed benchmark; ERM and 14 DG algorithms
evaluation_protocol: Controlled multi-algorithm DG comparison with explicit model-selection strategies
main_finding: Shows carefully implemented and tuned ERM is a very strong baseline and that many DG gains shrink under controlled evaluation.
limitation: Benchmarks are not remote-sensing-specific.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct methodological support for our finding that DG-AUG-V2 and RSC do not consistently beat ERM.

authors: Maryam Rahnemoonfar; Tashnim Chowdhury; Argho Sarkar; Debvrat Varshney; Mohammad Yari; Robin R. Murphy
title: FloodNet: A High Resolution Aerial Imagery Dataset for Post Flood Scene Understanding
method: Benchmark for image classification, semantic segmentation, and visual question answering
evaluation_protocol: Flooded vs non-flooded scene understanding and pixel-level flood semantics
main_finding: Introduces high-resolution post-Hurricane-Harvey UAV imagery and explicitly distinguishes natural water from flooded roads/buildings.
limitation: Established 2021 benchmark; classification taxonomy does not directly include our Desert class.
relevance_to_our_work: Our independent external UAV benchmark and the source of the segmentation masks used for shortcut analysis.

authors: Kaiyang Zhou; Yongxin Yang; Yu Qiao; Tao Xiang
title: Domain Generalization with MixStyle
main_finding: Mixes instance-level feature statistics to synthesize implicit domains and increase source-domain diversity.
limitation: Original benchmarks differ substantially from remote sensing and climate imagery.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for the MixStyle variants we tested.

authors: Robert Geirhos; Jörn-Henrik Jacobsen; Claudio Michaelis; Richard Zemel; Wieland Brendel; Matthias Bethge; Felix A. Wichmann
title: Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks
main_finding: Frames many benchmark-to-real-world failures as models learning predictive but non-robust shortcut decision rules.
limitation: General conceptual framework rather than remote-sensing specific quantitative evidence.
relevance_to_our_work: Core conceptual framework for interpreting our ordinary-water/non-flooded-road contextual shortcut evidence.

authors: Zeyi Huang; Haohan Wang; Eric P. Xing; Dong Huang
title: Self-Challenging Improves Cross-Domain Generalization
main_finding: Suppresses dominant predictive features during training to encourage alternative features that may generalize better across domains.
limitation: Original evidence comes from standard DG benchmarks, not heterogeneous remote-sensing sources.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for our RSC implementation and multi-seed evaluation.

authors: Christos Kyrkou; Theocharis Theocharides
title: EmergencyNet: Efficient Aerial Image Classification for Drone-Based Emergency Monitoring Using Atrous Convolutional Feature Fusion
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: Lightweight CNN with atrous convolutional feature fusion
evaluation_protocol: Emergency/disaster aerial image classification with deployment-efficiency analysis
main_finding: Shows efficient UAV disaster classification can retain strong accuracy while substantially reducing computational requirements.
limitation: Focuses on efficient within-benchmark classification rather than source-disjoint robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Important UAV disaster-classification baseline and application motivation.

authors: Mark Sandler; Andrew Howard; Menglong Zhu; Andrey Zhmoginov; Liang-Chieh Chen
title: MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
evaluation_protocol: Image classification and downstream transfer benchmarks
main_finding: Introduces inverted residual blocks and linear bottlenecks for efficient deep feature extraction.
limitation: Architecture paper does not address remote-sensing domain shift directly.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for the pretrained backbone used throughout our primary transfer-learning experiments.

authors: Ramprasaath R. Selvaraju; Michael Cogswell; Abhishek Das; Ramakrishna Vedantam; Devi Parikh; Dhruv Batra
title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-Based Localization
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
main_finding: Uses target-class gradients flowing into convolutional features to produce spatial explanations for CNN predictions.
limitation: Saliency/localization does not establish causal dependence.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational method for our 27 frozen Grad-CAM heatmaps.
